subject: Endocrine
vignette: A 32-year-old woman has 4 months of cold intolerance, decreased sweating, and a 6-kg weight gain despite eating less. She also reports constipation and low energy. Serum TSH is 14 µIU/mL and free T4 is 0.5 ng/dL. Her serum sodium is 132 mEq/L.
question: Which of the following best explains the weight gain in this patient?

options.text: Increased synthesis of Na+/K+-ATPase raising basal metabolic rate
Increased LDL receptor expression causing cholesterol deposition in adipose tissue
Decreased basal metabolic rate with reduced calorigenesis
Increased GI motility with enhanced nutrient absorption
Increased β-adrenergic activity raising resting energy expenditure

explanation_correct: Primary hypothyroidism (high TSH, low free T4) reduces basal metabolic rate and calorigenesis, so weight is gained even with reduced intake. Thyroid hormone normally increases synthesis of Na+/K+-ATPase, which raises BMR and oxygen consumption; its deficiency produces the opposite effect. The mild hyponatremia reflects decreased free water clearance. This contrasts with hyperthyroidism, in which increased Na+/K+-ATPase synthesis raises BMR and causes weight loss despite increased appetite.

explanation_incorrect.A: This is the hyperthyroid mechanism: increased Na+/K+-ATPase raises BMR and calorigenesis, producing heat intolerance and weight loss, not weight gain.
explanation_incorrect.B: Hypothyroidism reduces LDL receptor expression and causes hypercholesterolemia; LDL receptor changes do not drive adipose weight gain.
explanation_incorrect.D: Hypothyroidism decreases GI motility and causes constipation; increased motility and hyperdefecation are features of hyperthyroidism.
explanation_incorrect.E: Increased β-adrenergic activity causes the tremor, tachycardia, and anxiety of thyrotoxicosis and would increase energy expenditure rather than promote weight gain.

educationalObjective: Hypothyroid weight gain results from a reduced basal metabolic rate, whereas thyroid hormone excess raises Na+/K+-ATPase and BMR to cause weight loss.

subject: Endocrine
vignette: A 45-year-old woman with primary hypothyroidism has dry, cool skin, coarse brittle hair, brittle nails, and painless puffiness around the eyes and over the shins that does not pit. A colleague with Graves disease has warm, moist skin, fine hair, separation of the nail from the nail bed, and thickened skin over the anterior shins.
question: Which mechanism underlies the nonpitting edema in the hypothyroid patient?

options.text: Increased interstitial glycosaminoglycans raising osmotic pressure and water retention
Increased sympathetic stimulation of the superior tarsal muscle
Lymphocyte-mediated cytokines stimulating retroorbital fibroblasts
Reduced Na+/K+-ATPase activity in renal tubular epithelium
Granulomatous inflammation with giant cells infiltrating the dermis

explanation_correct: Hypothyroidism increases glycosaminoglycan (GAG) deposition in interstitial spaces; these hydrophilic molecules raise osmotic pressure and cause water retention, producing generalized nonpitting edema (myxedema) and puffy facies. Dry, cool skin with coarse brittle hair and diffuse alopecia reflects reduced blood flow and keratinization. Pretibial myxedema in Graves disease is a separate, localized depot of GAGs stimulated by thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulin. Recognizing nonpitting myxedema as a GAG/osmotic phenomenon, rather than a renal sodium problem, is the key distinction.

explanation_incorrect.B: Increased sympathetic tone to the superior tarsal muscle causes lid lag and lid retraction in thyrotoxicosis, not nonpitting edema.
explanation_incorrect.C: Retroorbital fibroblast stimulation by cytokines produces Graves ophthalmopathy with exophthalmos, not generalized myxedema.
explanation_incorrect.D: Altered free water clearance in hypothyroidism explains hyponatremia; it is not the mechanism of interstitial GAG deposition.
explanation_incorrect.E: Granulomatous inflammation characterizes subacute (de Quervain) thyroiditis and is not a feature of hypothyroid skin changes.

educationalObjective: Nonpitting myxedema in hypothyroidism results from interstitial glycosaminoglycan accumulation and osmotic water retention, distinct from Graves pretibial myxedema.

subject: Endocrine
vignette: A 27-year-old man with Graves disease notices that his eyes have a 'staring' appearance and that the upper lids fail to follow a downward-moving finger. Examination shows lid retraction and mild proptosis. Thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulin is elevated.
question: Which of the following best explains the lid lag and lid retraction in this patient?

options.text: Hydrophilic GAG deposition within extraocular muscles causing muscle swelling
Periorbital edema from hypothyroid GAG accumulation in the eyelids
Compression of the optic nerve by an enlarged retroorbital mass
Increased sympathetic stimulation of the superior tarsal muscle
Autoimmune destruction of the lacrimal glands reducing tear production

explanation_correct: In thyrotoxicosis, increased sympathetic stimulation contracts the superior tarsal (Müller) muscle, producing lid retraction and lid lag on downward gaze. This is a distinct phenomenon from Graves ophthalmopathy, in which thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulin activates orbital fibroblasts and T-cell cytokines drive hydrophilic GAG secretion, muscle inflammation, adipocyte accumulation, and exophthalmos. The patient has both processes, but only the sympathetic mechanism explains the lid lag. Glucocorticoids are used to treat the inflammatory orbitopathy.

explanation_incorrect.A: GAG deposition in retroorbital tissues produces exophthalmos and ophthalmopathy, not the lid lag/retraction of increased sympathetic tone.
explanation_incorrect.B: Hypothyroid periorbital edema causes puffy lids but does not produce the lid lag or staring gaze seen here.
explanation_incorrect.C: Optic nerve compression would cause visual field defects or vision loss rather than isolated lid lag.
explanation_incorrect.E: Lacrimal gland destruction is not a feature of Graves disease and would cause dry eyes, not lid retraction.

educationalObjective: Lid lag and retraction in hyperthyroidism reflect increased sympathetic stimulation of the superior tarsal muscle, whereas exophthalmos results from retroorbital GAG deposition and inflammation.

subject: Endocrine
vignette: A 52-year-old woman with long-standing hypothyroidism has proximal muscle weakness, a small lump that rises on the deltoid when tapped with a hammer, and numbness in both hands. Her creatine kinase is elevated. A second patient with thyrotoxicosis has similar proximal weakness but a normal creatine kinase and a recent low-trauma vertebral fracture.
question: Which pairing of musculoskeletal findings best fits these two patients?

options.text: Hypothyroid myopathy with normal CK; thyrotoxic myopathy with elevated CK
Hypothyroid myopathy with elevated CK and myoedema; thyrotoxic myopathy with normal CK and osteoporosis
Hypothyroid myopathy with myoedema and osteoporosis; thyrotoxic myopathy with elevated CK
Hypothyroid myopathy with brisk reflexes; thyrotoxic myopathy with delayed reflex relaxation
Hypothyroid myopathy with T3-driven osteoclast stimulation; thyrotoxic myopathy with carpal tunnel syndrome

explanation_correct: Hypothyroid myopathy causes proximal weakness with an elevated CK, myoedema (a transient mound of muscle after percussion), and carpal tunnel syndrome from interstitial GAG deposition. Thyrotoxic myopathy also causes proximal weakness but typically has a normal CK. Excess T3 stimulates osteoclast differentiation and bone resorption with calcium release, producing osteoporosis and an increased fracture rate. The lump after tapping and the fracture therefore point in opposite thyroid directions.

explanation_incorrect.A: The CK pattern is reversed: hypothyroid myopathy has elevated CK, while thyrotoxic myopathy has a normal CK.
explanation_incorrect.C: Myoedema is hypothyroid; osteoporosis and increased fracture risk are thyrotoxic, and thyrotoxic myopathy does not raise CK.
explanation_incorrect.D: Reflexes are reversed: hypothyroidism gives delayed, slow-relaxing reflexes and hyperthyroidism gives brisk reflexes.
explanation_incorrect.E: T3-driven osteoclast stimulation and carpal tunnel syndrome belong to hyperthyroidism and hypothyroidism respectively, the reverse of this option.

educationalObjective: Hypothyroid myopathy features elevated CK, myoedema, and carpal tunnel syndrome, whereas thyrotoxic myopathy has normal CK and T3-driven osteoporosis with increased fractures.

subject: Endocrine
vignette: A 41-year-old man with untreated Graves disease has a resting heart rate of 112/min, bounding pulses, and a blood pressure of 156/64 mm Hg. He has intermittent palpitations, and ECG shows atrial fibrillation. He reports dyspnea on exertion but his left ventricle is normal-sized on echocardiography.
question: Which of the following best explains the tachycardia and systolic hypertension in this patient?

options.text: Increased LDL receptor expression expanding plasma volume
Increased phospholamban expression enhancing diastolic relaxation
Reduced β-adrenergic receptor number triggering reflex tachycardia
Decreased sarcolemmal ATPase activity prolonging ventricular contraction
Increased β-adrenergic receptor number/sensitivity with increased cardiac ATPase and decreased phospholamban

explanation_correct: Thyroid hormone increases the number and sensitivity of β-adrenergic receptors, increases expression of cardiac sarcolemmal ATPase, and decreases phospholamban expression. The net effect is increased chronotropy, contractility, and stroke volume with reduced afterload, producing tachycardia, palpitations, arrhythmias such as atrial fibrillation, and systolic hypertension with a wide pulse pressure. Hypothyroidism produces the opposite picture: bradycardia and decreased cardiac output with dyspnea on exertion. These changes are direct thyroid hormone effects, not secondary to lipid abnormalities.

explanation_incorrect.A: LDL receptor expression is reduced in hypothyroidism and affects cholesterol, not cardiac contractility or pulse pressure.
explanation_incorrect.B: Thyroid hormone decreases phospholamban expression; increased phospholamban would not explain the hyperdynamic circulation.
explanation_incorrect.C: β-adrenergic receptor number and sensitivity are increased, not reduced, in hyperthyroidism.
explanation_incorrect.D: Cardiac sarcolemmal ATPase expression is increased, not decreased, in the hyperthyroid state.

educationalObjective: Hyperthyroid tachycardia, atrial fibrillation, and systolic hypertension arise from increased β-adrenergic receptors, increased cardiac ATPase, and decreased phospholamban.

subject: Endocrine
vignette: A 38-year-old woman has fatigue, depressed mood, cold intolerance, delayed relaxation of her deep tendon reflexes, and abnormal uterine bleeding. TSH is 18 µIU/mL, free T4 is 0.4 ng/dL, and total cholesterol is 265 mg/dL. Her brother has anxiety, a fine tremor, brisk reflexes, gynecomastia, TSH below 0.01 µIU/mL, and free T4 of 3.2 ng/dL.
question: Which of the following best accounts for the difference in lipid levels between these two patients?

options.text: Hypothyroidism increases LDL receptor expression, clearing cholesterol and lowering serum levels
Hyperthyroidism decreases LDL clearance, raising HDL and total cholesterol
Hypothyroidism decreases LDL receptor expression causing hypercholesterolemia; hyperthyroidism lowers LDL, HDL, and total cholesterol
Hyperthyroidism raises total cholesterol through increased VLDL despite increased LDL receptor activity
Hypothyroidism selectively raises HDL while lowering LDL and total cholesterol

explanation_correct: Primary hypothyroidism reduces LDL receptor expression, decreasing clearance of LDL and producing hypercholesterolemia; this contributes to atherosclerosis. Hyperthyroidism lowers LDL, HDL, and total cholesterol. The accompanying findings reinforce the direction: hypothyroidism causes lethargy, depressed mood, delayed reflex relaxation, and abnormal uterine bleeding, while hyperthyroidism causes anxiety, fine tremor from increased β-adrenergic activity, brisk reflexes, and gynecomastia with abnormal uterine bleeding and infertility in both states.

explanation_incorrect.A: The direction is reversed: hypothyroidism reduces LDL receptor expression and raises, rather than lowers, serum cholesterol.
explanation_incorrect.B: Hyperthyroidism accelerates lipid clearance and lowers LDL, HDL, and total cholesterol.
explanation_incorrect.D: Hyperthyroidism does not raise total cholesterol; the net effect of thyroid excess is a reduction in all measured lipid fractions.
explanation_incorrect.E: Hypothyroidism raises LDL and total cholesterol and is not characterized by selective HDL elevation with lower LDL.

educationalObjective: Reduced LDL receptor expression in hypothyroidism causes hypercholesterolemia, while hyperthyroidism lowers LDL, HDL, and total cholesterol along with distinct neuropsychiatric and reflex findings.
